simple: a device asks for attention by writing a small value to a special address instead of raising a wire.
analogy: a note pushed through the office's mail slot.
precise: a PCI capability (ID 05h) holding a message address, a message data value and an enable bit; to interrupt, the function performs a posted memory write of the data to the address. On x86 the address selects a local APIC and the data carries the vector.
source: D1 of F4-08 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Local Bus Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: MSI capability structure; command register interrupt-disable bit)); D3 of F4-08 (Intel, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual", Volume 3 (curriculum C7 reading: APIC; message signalled interrupts, message address and data format). Intel 82093AA I/O APIC datasheet for the redirection entries) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: MSI with a table of many messages, one per event source.
analogy: a pad of pre-addressed notes, one per class.
precise: a PCI capability (ID 11h) pointing into a BAR at a table of 16-byte entries (address, data, vector control with a mask bit) and a pending bit array (PBA).
source: D2 of F4-08 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Express Base Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: MSI-X capability and table structure; ordering of posted writes; requester ID)); L1 of F4-08 (L1 — Linux UAPI header <linux/pci_regs.h> as installed in the build container (opened in this build by msicheck.cpp; tier 4): PCI_CAP_ID_MSI, PCI_MSI_*, PCI_MSIX_*) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the MSI-X list of interrupts a device wanted to send while they were masked.
analogy: the pile of notes that waited behind a closed mail slot.
precise: an array of bits in a BAR of an MSI-X function, one per table entry; a bit is set when the function wants to send a masked vector's message and is cleared when it is sent after unmasking.
source: D2 of F4-08 (PCI-SIG, "PCI Express Base Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: MSI-X capability and table structure; ordering of posted writes; requester ID)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one number for every interrupt input of every IOAPIC in the machine.
analogy: a single numbering of all the bell wires in all the school's switchboards.
precise: the ACPI flat interrupt number space: each IOAPIC in the MADT has a GSI base, and its input n is GSI base + n; ISA IRQs map to GSIs through interrupt source overrides.
source: D5 of F4-08 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification": MADT, interrupt source override structures, global system interrupts) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the address a device is told to use for a buffer.
analogy: the shelf number written on the driver's note.
precise: an address in a DMA domain's address space, translated by the IOMMU to a physical address; without an IOMMU it equals the physical address.
source: D4 of F4-08 (Intel, "Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O Architecture Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: root and context tables, second-level translation, invalidation, fault reporting; the ACPI DMAR table it defines)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one set of mappings shared by the devices put in it.
analogy: one list of allowed shelves.
precise: in VT-d, the address space named by a domain ID in a context entry, with its own second-level page tables.
source: D4 of F4-08 (Intel, "Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O Architecture Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: root and context tables, second-level translation, invalidation, fault reporting; the ACPI DMAR table it defines)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the ACPI table that says where the IOMMU units are and which devices each one covers.
analogy: the visitor desk's list of which gate covers which corridor.
precise: the DMA Remapping Reporting table defined by the VT-d specification: host address width, flags, and DRHD structures (register base, segment, INCLUDE_PCI_ALL flag, device scope entries), plus reserved memory regions (RMRR).
source: D4 of F4-08 (Intel, "Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O Architecture Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: root and context tables, second-level translation, invalidation, fault reporting; the ACPI DMAR table it defines)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the IOMMU's per-device record of which translation tables to use.
analogy: the line in the gate's book for one visitor badge: which floor plan applies.
precise: a 128-bit VT-d entry indexed by device and function in a per-bus context table (reached from the root table): present bit, translation type, address width, domain ID and the address of the second-level page table.
source: D4 of F4-08 (Intel, "Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O Architecture Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: root and context tables, second-level translation, invalidation, fault reporting; the ACPI DMAR table it defines)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the IOMMU's cache of recent address translations.
analogy: the gate guard's memory of badges already checked today.
precise: the translation cache of an IOMMU unit; after changing a mapping, software must invalidate the affected entries (globally, per domain or per page) through the invalidation registers or queue before reusing the address.
source: D4 of F4-08 (Intel, "Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O Architecture Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: root and context tables, second-level translation, invalidation, fault reporting; the ACPI DMAR table it defines)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the IOMMU's note about a request it refused.
analogy: the gatekeeper's log book line.
precise: a 128-bit register holding the faulting page address, the requester's source ID, the read/write type and a fault reason code, with a "fault" bit the software clears by writing 1.
source: D4 of F4-08 (Intel, "Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O Architecture Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: root and context tables, second-level translation, invalidation, fault reporting; the ACPI DMAR table it defines)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the kernel functions a driver calls to turn a buffer into an address a device may use.
analogy: the office issuing a visitor badge for one room and taking it back afterwards.
precise: a layer that maps a CPU buffer to a bus address (an IOVA through the IOMMU, or the physical address with identity mapping) for a given device and direction, and unmaps it when the transfer is done; drivers never hand physical addresses to devices directly.
source: the lab's own dma.h/dma.cc layer of F4-08, modelled on the Linux kernel's DMA API (Linux documentation not opened in this build); D4 of F4-08 (Intel, "Intel Virtualization Technology for Directed I/O Architecture Specification" (curriculum C7 reading: root and context tables, second-level translation, invalidation, fault reporting; the ACPI DMAR table it defines)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the chip that runs every USB conversation for the computer.
analogy: the reception desk.
precise: a PCI device implementing the eXtensible Host Controller Interface: capability, operational, runtime and doorbell registers plus rings of 16-byte TRBs in memory, covering USB 1.x, 2.0 and 3.x devices.
source: D3 of F4-09 (Intel, "eXtensible Host Controller Interface for Universal Serial Bus (xHCI) Specification" (curriculum C8 reading: registers; device, slot and endpoint contexts; command, event and transfer rings; Host Controller Initialization; Device Slot Management; USB Legacy Support capability)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small table a device sends to describe itself.
analogy: the self-description form.
precise: a structure starting with bLength and bDescriptorType; the device descriptor (18 bytes), the configuration descriptor (9 bytes) followed by interface, endpoint and class descriptors, read with GET_DESCRIPTOR.
source: D1 of F4-09 (USB Implementers Forum, "Universal Serial Bus Specification, Revision 2.0", chapter 9 "USB Device Framework" (curriculum C8 reading); chapters 5 and 8 for transfer types and the protocol layer); L1 of F4-09 (L1 — Linux UAPI header <linux/usb/ch9.h> as installed in the build container (opened in this build by usbcheck.cpp; tier 4)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one numbered mailbox inside a device, for one direction.
analogy: one of the visitor's in-trays or out-trays.
precise: an address 0–15 with a direction bit (bit 7 = IN, toward the host) and a transfer type: control, bulk, interrupt or isochronous. Endpoint 0 is the bidirectional control endpoint every device has.
source: D1 of F4-09 (USB Implementers Forum, "Universal Serial Bus Specification, Revision 2.0", chapter 9 "USB Device Framework" (curriculum C8 reading); chapters 5 and 8 for transfer types and the protocol layer) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one 16-byte work order on a ring.
analogy: one ticket on the desk's spike.
precise: parameter (8 bytes), status (4) and control (4, with the TRB type in bits 15:10 and the cycle bit in bit 0); used for commands, transfers and events.
source: D3 of F4-09 (Intel, "eXtensible Host Controller Interface for Universal Serial Bus (xHCI) Specification" (curriculum C8 reading: registers; device, slot and endpoint contexts; command, event and transfer rings; Host Controller Initialization; Device Slot Management; USB Legacy Support capability)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one bit in each ring entry that says whose turn it is.
analogy: a card turned face up or face down to show which round it belongs to.
precise: bit 0 of a TRB's control word; the producer writes entries with its current cycle state, the consumer accepts entries matching its own, and both toggle their state when passing a Link TRB with Toggle Cycle set (or wrapping an event ring).
source: D3 of F4-09 (Intel, "eXtensible Host Controller Interface for Universal Serial Bus (xHCI) Specification" (curriculum C8 reading: registers; device, slot and endpoint contexts; command, event and transfer rings; Host Controller Initialization; Device Slot Management; USB Legacy Support capability)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the controller's memory record of one USB device: its slot and its endpoints.
analogy: the file the office keeps on one visitor, with a page per door they may use.
precise: a structure of a slot context and up to 31 endpoint contexts, owned by the xHC once its address is in the device context base address array; software changes it only through input contexts and commands (Address Device, Configure Endpoint).
source: D3 of F4-09 (Intel, "eXtensible Host Controller Interface for Universal Serial Bus (xHCI) Specification" (curriculum C8 reading: registers; device, slot and endpoint contexts; command, event and transfer rings; Host Controller Initialization; Device Slot Management; USB Legacy Support capability)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a fixed, simple keyboard and mouse report format that works without parsing a report descriptor.
analogy: the "short form" every keyboard can fill in.
precise: for a keyboard, an 8-byte report: modifier bits, a reserved byte and up to six key usage codes from the HID Usage Tables; selected with SET_PROTOCOL(0).
source: D4 of F4-09 (USB Implementers Forum, "Device Class Definition for Human Interface Devices (HID)" (boot protocol, SET_PROTOCOL, SET_IDLE) and "HID Usage Tables" (keyboard usage page)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how a USB stick carries disk commands.
analogy: a sealed command envelope, the goods, then a receipt.
precise: a 31-byte Command Block Wrapper ("USBC") on the bulk OUT endpoint holding a SCSI command, an optional data phase, and a 13-byte Command Status Wrapper ("USBS") on bulk IN with a matching tag and a status.
source: D5 of F4-09 (USB Implementers Forum, "USB Mass Storage Class Bulk-Only Transport"; INCITS T10, "SCSI Primary Commands" and "SCSI Block Commands" (INQUIRY, REQUEST SENSE, READ CAPACITY(10), READ(10), WRITE(10); sense keys and ASC codes)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the device's explanation of why the last command failed.
analogy: the note the clerk hands back saying why the request was refused.
precise: the response to REQUEST SENSE: in fixed format, a sense key (byte 2, low nibble), an additional sense code (byte 12) and qualifier (byte 13); for example key 5 with code 0x21 means "illegal request: logical block address out of range".
source: D5 of F4-09 (USB Implementers Forum, "USB Mass Storage Class Bulk-Only Transport"; INCITS T10, "SCSI Primary Commands" and "SCSI Block Commands" (INQUIRY, REQUEST SENSE, READ CAPACITY(10), READ(10), WRITE(10); sense keys and ASC codes)); L2 of F4-09 (L2 — glibc/Linux header <scsi/scsi.h> as installed in the build container (opened in this build by usbcheck.cpp; tier 4)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a recording of every USB packet a Linux host exchanges, readable with Wireshark.
analogy: a CCTV recording of the school entrance.
precise: Linux's USB monitoring interface; captures of URB submissions and completions with setup packets and data, saved as pcap files. In this course's labs the capture comes from QEMU's own USB packet capture option, a similar format read with tshark.
source: R4 of F4-09 (R4 — lab run, step capture: capture.out, capture.log (tshark 4.2.2 on QEMU's keyboard capture)); the Linux usbmon documentation was not opened in this build — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a circular list in memory where the driver and the card hand packet buffers to each other.
analogy: the post room's pigeonholes with "full" and "empty" flags.
precise: an array of 16-byte descriptors (buffer address, length, status, errors) with a head register advanced by the NIC and a tail register written by the driver; the descriptor-done (DD) bit marks the ones the NIC has finished.
source: D1 of F4-10 (Intel, "PCI/PCI-X Family of Gigabit Ethernet Controllers Software Developer's Manual" (8254x) (curriculum C9 reading: initialization, receive and transmit descriptor rings, EEPROM and MAC address, interrupt cause registers, statistics)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: asking the local network "who has this IP address?" to learn its hardware address.
analogy: shouting a name in the corridor to find which room someone is in.
precise: the Address Resolution Protocol: a broadcast request and a unicast reply mapping an IPv4 address to an Ethernet MAC address, cached by the requester.
source: D2 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 826, "An Ethernet Address Resolution Protocol") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a 16-bit sum that lets the receiver notice a damaged header.
analogy: the total written at the bottom of a page.
precise: the one's complement of the one's complement sum of 16-bit big-endian words; IPv4 covers its header, UDP and TCP cover a pseudo-header (addresses, protocol, length) plus their segment.
source: D3 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 791, "Internet Protocol", and RFC 1071, "Computing the Internet Checksum") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how a machine gets an IP address when it joins a network.
analogy: asking the office for a desk number on the first day.
precise: a UDP protocol (client port 68, server 67): DISCOVER, OFFER, REQUEST, ACK, with options for mask, router, DNS server and lease time.
source: D5 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 2131, "Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol" (and RFC 2132 for the options)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: TCP numbers every byte; the receiver says which byte it expects next.
analogy: page numbers and receipts.
precise: 32-bit numbers starting at an initial sequence number chosen per connection; ACK = next expected byte (cumulative); comparisons use modulo-232 arithmetic.
source: D6 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 9293, "Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how long TCP waits for a receipt before sending again.
analogy: the kitchen timer for the oldest unsigned page.
precise: computed from smoothed round-trip time SRTT and variation RTTVAR (RTO = SRTT + 4 × RTTVAR, at least 1 s per RFC 6298), doubled after each timeout; the timer must run whenever data is unacknowledged.
source: D8 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 6298, "Computing TCP's Retransmission Timer" (rules 2.1–2.5 and 5.1–5.7 as cited)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: resending a missing segment as soon as three duplicate receipts show it is missing.
analogy: three receipts in a row saying "still waiting for page 12".
precise: on the third duplicate ACK the sender retransmits the first unacknowledged segment without waiting for the RTO and halves its congestion window (RFC 5681).
source: D7 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 5681, "TCP Congestion Control") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how much unacknowledged data the sender allows itself to have in flight.
analogy: how many letters you post before waiting for replies, raised while all goes well and cut when letters get lost.
precise: cwnd, a sender-side limit in bytes: the sender may have at most min(cwnd, receiver window) bytes unacknowledged; it grows in slow start and congestion avoidance and is reduced after loss (to one segment after a timeout, about half after fast retransmit).
source: D7 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 5681, "TCP Congestion Control") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: never measure round-trip time on a packet that was sent twice.
analogy: if you posted the same letter twice, you cannot tell which copy the reply answers.
precise: RTT samples are taken only from segments that were not retransmitted, and the backed-off RTO is kept until a new sample is obtained.
source: D8 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 6298, "Computing TCP's Retransmission Timer" (rules 2.1–2.5 and 5.1–5.7 as cited)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the largest piece of data one TCP packet may carry.
analogy: the most pages that fit in one envelope.
precise: a TCP option sent in the SYN announcing the largest segment payload the sender of the option can receive; on Ethernet usually 1460 bytes (1500 MTU minus 20 bytes of IPv4 and 20 of TCP header).
source: D6 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 9293, "Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: QEMU's built-in fake network that connects a guest to the host's sockets.
analogy: a receptionist who passes your letters on under her own name.
precise: QEMU's "user" network backend (libslirp): a virtual router, DHCP server and DNS forwarder at 10.0.2.x that translates guest TCP and UDP into host socket calls; it does not pass ICMP from the host to the guest, and host-to-guest connections need port forwarding.
source: D10 of F4-10 (QEMU documentation: user-mode networking (hostfwd, guestfwd with cmd:), network filters (filter-dump and the others), the e1000 device) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an acknowledgement that repeats the previous one because a later segment arrived out of order.
analogy: a reply saying "I still need page 6" each time a later page arrives.
precise: an ACK carrying no data and no window change whose acknowledgement number equals the previous highest; three in a row trigger fast retransmit.
source: D7 of F4-10 (IETF RFC 5681, "TCP Congestion Control") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the table that says where the basic power-management registers are.
analogy: the first page of the caretaker's binder: where the main switches are.
precise: the ACPI table with signature "FACP": I/O addresses of the PM1 event and control blocks, the PM timer and the GPE blocks, the SCI interrupt number, SMI_CMD with the ACPI_ENABLE value, flags, and the address of the DSDT.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the tree of all names the AML defines.
analogy: the binder's table of contents.
precise: a hierarchy of 4-character name segments from the root \ (for example \_SB.PCI0.S08), built by loading the definition blocks.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the one interrupt all ACPI events share.
analogy: the night bell; the caretaker's log says which door rang it.
precise: a level-triggered, shareable interrupt (on PCs usually ISA IRQ 9) raised by fixed events (power button, PM timer carry) and general-purpose events (GPEs) whose enable bits are set.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: "soft off", and the package that says which number means it on this machine.
analogy: "write 0 in box S5, pull lever 13".
precise: \_S5 is a Package whose first two elements are the SLP_TYP values for PM1a_CNT and PM1b_CNT; writing SLP_TYP with SLP_EN (bit 13) enters the state.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list saying which interrupt wire each PCI slot's pin is connected to.
analogy: "room 4's bell goes to input 21".
precise: an object under a PCI root bridge returning a package of {address (device << 16 | 0xFFFF), pin (0–3 for INTA–INTD), source (a link device or 0), source index (a GSI when source is 0)}.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a programmable interrupt router described in AML.
analogy: a switchboard plug whose position the binder describes.
precise: a device with _HID PNP0C0F and _PRS (possible resources), _CRS (current), _SRS (set) and _DIS (disable) objects.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the length field at the start of every AML object that has a body.
analogy: the page count written at the top of each section of the binder.
precise: an AML encoding of 1 to 4 bytes: bits 7-6 of the lead byte give the number of following bytes; with none, bits 5-0 are the length; otherwise bits 3-0 are the low nibble and each following byte adds 8 bits. The length includes the PkgLength bytes.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a free-running counter at a fixed 3.579545 MHz that ACPI machines provide.
analogy: the caretaker's wall clock, always ticking at the same rate.
precise: the ACPI power-management timer: a 24-bit (or 32-bit, by an FADT flag) counter in I/O space at the FADT's PM_TMR_BLK, which sets TMR_STS when its top bit changes.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the I/O port through which the OS asks the firmware to hand over power management.
analogy: the bell to call the caretaker before taking over his keys.
precise: an FADT field holding an I/O port; writing the FADT's ACPI_ENABLE value there raises a system management interrupt in which the firmware switches the chipset to ACPI mode and sets SCI_EN.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a 7-character device ID such as PNP0A08 squeezed into 32 bits.
analogy: a catalogue number written in shorthand.
precise: a compressed ID: three letters of 5 bits each ('A' = 1) in the first 16 bits read big-endian, then four hexadecimal digits; used for _HID and _CID integers.
source: D1 of F4-11 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (curriculum C10 reading: FADT; PM1 event and control registers; the SCI; "ACPI Machine Language (AML) Specification"; "Device Configuration" (_HID, _CRS, _PRS, _PRT); "Waking and Sleeping"; resource descriptors; Embedded Controller, battery and thermal chapters)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of an OS that runs the firmware's AML methods.
analogy: the person who can follow the binder's procedures step by step.
precise: a byte-code interpreter for AML (ACPICA, uACPI) that loads definition blocks into a namespace, evaluates methods and accesses hardware through OperationRegions, needing an OS services layer (memory mapping, locks, port and PCI access, interrupt installation, timers).
source: D2 of F4-11 (ACPICA project, "ACPI Component Architecture User Guide and Programmer Reference" (OS Services Layer) and the uACPI project documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the PCI device that moves sound data and commands between memory and the audio chips.
analogy: the cable room between the office and the sound desk.
precise: a PCI function of class 04h subclass 03h whose BAR0 holds global registers, the CORB and RIRB registers and one descriptor per stream; it drives the HD Audio link to up to 15 codecs.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the chip that turns numbers into an analog signal (and back).
analogy: the sound desk itself.
precise: a device on the HD Audio link at an address 0–14, described as a tree of nodes: a root node, function groups and widgets, each read with "get parameter" verbs.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one command to one part of a codec.
analogy: a numbered slip in the tray.
precise: a 32-bit word: codec address (bits 31–28), node ID (27–20) and a 20-bit verb with payload: either a 12-bit verb and an 8-bit payload or a 4-bit verb and a 16-bit payload. Every verb gets exactly one 32-bit response.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the two rings in memory for commands out and answers back.
analogy: the note tray and the reply tray.
precise: the Command Outbound Ring Buffer (up to 256 4-byte verbs; software advances the write pointer, the controller the read pointer) and the Response Inbound Ring Buffer (up to 256 8-byte entries: the response and a word with the codec address and a "solicited or not" bit; the controller advances its write pointer).
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one building block inside a codec.
analogy: one unit on the sound desk: a player, a mixer, a socket.
precise: a node of a function group with a type (audio output converter, audio input, mixer, selector, pin complex, power, volume knob, beep) in its Audio Widget Capabilities parameter, and a connection list naming the widgets that feed it.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the codec widget that connects to a jack or a speaker.
analogy: the socket on the sound desk that a speaker cable plugs into.
precise: an HD Audio widget of type 4 with pin capabilities (input, output, presence detect, EAPD) and a configuration default register written by the board maker that describes its device, location, connector and colour.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of memory pieces a stream plays, in order.
analogy: the card saying where each piece of the tape loop starts and how long it is.
precise: an array of 16-byte entries (64-bit address, 32-bit length, a flags word whose bit 0 is "interrupt on completion"), 128-byte aligned, at least two entries; the stream walks it cyclically up to the last valid index.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number that says how fast, how many bits and how many channels.
analogy: the tape speed written on the label.
precise: a 16-bit word (base rate 48 or 44.1 kHz, multiply, divide, sample size, channels minus one) written identically to the stream descriptor and to the converter widget (Figure 3).
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number that tells the codec which stream on the link is meant for it.
analogy: the channel number on the announcement system.
precise: a stream number 1-15 written to the stream descriptor's control register and, with Set Converter Stream/Channel, to the converter widget; data blocks on the link carry the tag. 0 means the converter listens to nothing.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how far the stream has got through its buffer, in bytes.
analogy: the counter on the tape player.
precise: a stream descriptor register holding the byte offset in the cyclic buffer of the data most recently sent on the link; it wraps to 0 after CBL bytes.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one of the equal parts an audio buffer is divided into, with an interrupt at the end of each.
analogy: one piece of the tape loop.
precise: a buffer descriptor list entry (or group of entries) with interrupt-on-completion set; period size trades interrupt rate against latency, and the driver refills a period after its completion interrupt.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a message a codec sends without being asked, for example when a jack is plugged in.
analogy: a reply slip in the tray that answers no question.
precise: a RIRB entry with bit 4 of its second word set, sent by a codec after the driver enables unsolicited responses on a widget; it carries a tag chosen by the driver and must not be matched to an outstanding verb.
source: D1 of F4-12 (Intel, "High Definition Audio Specification", revision 1.0a (curriculum C11 reading: controller registers, CORB/RIRB command rings, stream descriptors and buffer descriptor lists, stream format, codec verbs, parameters and the widget graph, the link protocol)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small security chip that keeps records nobody can roll back and keys nobody can copy out.
analogy: the porter with the sealed tally.
precise: a device implementing the TCG TPM 2.0 Library Specification: PCR banks, hierarchies of keys, a random number generator, sealed storage and signing (quotes), reached through a command/response interface.
source: D1 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "TPM 2.0 Library Specification", Parts 1–3 (curriculum C13 reading: architecture; PCRs and extend; command and response structures; TPM2_Startup, PCR_Read, PCR_Extend, GetRandom; response codes; password sessions)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a register you can only add to, never set.
analogy: the sealed tally.
precise: a hash-sized register, one per bank (SHA-256 here), reset to zero at power-on (PCRs 0–15 on PC clients) and changed only by extend: new = H(old ‖ digest).
source: D1 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "TPM 2.0 Library Specification", Parts 1–3 (curriculum C13 reading: architecture; PCRs and extend; command and response structures; TPM2_Startup, PCR_Read, PCR_Extend, GetRandom; response codes; password sessions)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the one way a PCR changes.
analogy: mixing the next name into the tally.
precise: TPM2_PCR_Extend replaces a PCR with the hash of its old value concatenated with a new digest; the order of extends matters and no command undoes one.
source: D1 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "TPM 2.0 Library Specification", Parts 1–3 (curriculum C13 reading: architecture; PCRs and extend; command and response structures; TPM2_Startup, PCR_Read, PCR_Extend, GetRandom; response codes; password sessions)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the list of what was measured, kept in ordinary memory.
analogy: the visitors' book.
precise: a table in memory (its address in the ACPI TPM2 table or from UEFI) with one entry per extend: PCR index, event type, the digest per bank and event data; the TCG PC Client Platform Firmware Profile defines the format.
source: D3 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "PC Client Platform Firmware Profile Specification" (curriculum C13 reading: event log format, event types, PCR usage, roots of trust)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: proving to someone else what your machine booted.
analogy: the inspector's check, with the porter's signature on the tally.
precise: the verifier receives the event log and a quote (PCR values signed by a TPM attestation key it trusts), replays the log and compares.
source: D1 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "TPM 2.0 Library Specification", Parts 1–3 (curriculum C13 reading: architecture; PCRs and extend; command and response structures; TPM2_Startup, PCR_Read, PCR_Extend, GetRandom; response codes; password sessions)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the register window through which commands go in and responses come out, byte by byte.
analogy: the porter's hatch.
precise: the TPM Interface Specification register set (one 4 KiB page per locality at 0xFED40000 + 0x1000 × locality: ACCESS, STS, DATA_FIFO, DID_VID …), defined in the PC Client Platform TPM Profile; CRB is the alternative, buffer-based interface.
source: D2 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "PC Client Platform TPM Profile (PTP) Specification" (curriculum C13 reading: TIS/FIFO and CRB interfaces, localities, register layout)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each boot stage checks the next stage's signature and refuses to run it if the check fails.
analogy: the porter turning away visitors without a valid pass.
precise: a boot chain in which every stage verifies a signature over the next against trusted keys before transferring control (UEFI Secure Boot is one form); unlike measured boot it enforces at boot time and records nothing for later verification.
source: D3 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "PC Client Platform Firmware Profile Specification" (curriculum C13 reading: event log format, event types, PCR usage, roots of trust)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the TPM interface that passes whole commands through a memory buffer instead of a byte FIFO.
analogy: a pigeonhole instead of a hatch.
precise: the PC Client PTP interface with a control area (request, status, cancel, start registers) and command and response buffers whose addresses it gives; used by most firmware TPMs. ACPI TPM2 start method 7.
source: D2 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "PC Client Platform TPM Profile (PTP) Specification" (curriculum C13 reading: TIS/FIFO and CRB interfaces, localities, register layout)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: which privilege level a TPM command comes from.
analogy: which door of the porter's lodge a request comes through.
precise: one of five TIS/CRB register pages (0-4); the TPM knows which locality sent a command and some PCRs (17-22, the dynamic-launch PCRs) can be reset or extended only from higher localities.
source: D2 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "PC Client Platform TPM Profile (PTP) Specification" (curriculum C13 reading: TIS/FIFO and CRB interfaces, localities, register layout)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the first code that measures, which nobody measured.
analogy: the porter's own honesty, on which the whole tally rests.
precise: the component trusted to make the first measurement (the core root of trust for measurement, usually an immutable firmware boot block); if it can be changed unnoticed, no later measurement can be trusted.
source: D3 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "PC Client Platform Firmware Profile Specification" (curriculum C13 reading: event log format, event types, PCR usage, roots of trust)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the ACPI table that says a TPM exists, which interface it uses and where the firmware's event log is.
analogy: the notice at the entrance saying where the porter's lodge is and where the visitors' book is kept.
precise: an ACPI table with signature "TPM2": platform class, control area address, start method (6 = TIS, 7 = CRB, among others) and, in newer revisions, the log area minimum length (LAML) and start address (LASA).
source: D7 of F4-13 (Trusted Computing Group, "TCG ACPI Specification" (the TPM2 table: start method, log area length and address)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
